thread:
maria: Heads-up: noticed a spike in cross-org API key usage after yesterday's CLI rollout. repro steps below.
jun: wait what spike? where are you seeing it?
maria: in the token-ops dashboard. lots of requests hitting org B keys from instances that should be org A.
laura: :eyes: can you paste the CLI command that was rolled out?
maria: yeah — the new default config changed so --org-context now falls back to env ORG_ID if not set. exact command we shipped: `redwood-cli auth login --default-context=env`
sam: oh no. that means machine agents without explicit org flag might pick up host env ORG_ID and use shared creds.
jun: can we see the logs?
maria: pasted sample from request logs:
```
2026-03-19T12:04:21Z GET /v1/keys/org-B HTTP/1.1 200 123ms x-api-key: sk-live-XXXX
2026-03-19T12:04:22Z POST /v1/infer org: org-A requester: ci-runner-7 status: 202
```
jun: looks like the CLI used key for org-B while the inference request claimed org-A. mismatch in auth header vs route org. weird.
security-bot: Alert: possible credential-scoping regression (severity: high). Attached correlation id: c0rr-789.
laura: immediate mitigation: roll back CLI default to previous behavior and revoke any session tokens issued after 2026-03-19T11:50Z.
sam: I can push a hotfix to config parsing in CLI in 10m. I'll also add a validation to fail if env ORG_ID and --org flag differ.
maria: I'm running quick audit to list all tokens minted during window. query: `select token, issuer, org, created_at from tokens where created_at > '2026-03-19T11:50:00Z'`
jun: check KMS access logs too. if a KMS unwrap happened for a different tenant, escalate.
maria: KMS logs show no unwrap calls for those tokens — looks like tokens were present in plain in a shared CI secret store.
laura: that suggests credential diffusion rather than KMS compromise. still treat as P1 until we confirm.
sam: pushed CLI patch `v1.2.9` -> pinned default to explicit-org-required. publishing release now. deploy-bot: release v1.2.9 deployed to canary at 2026-03-19T12:20Z :rocket:
jun: I'm triggering audit alert rules and adding temporary deny policies for any token used outside its org boundary. will add RBAC rule: `deny if request.auth.org != request.route.org` on gateway.
maria: confirmed revocations started. list of affected tokens (anonymized): `tok-***, tok-***, tok-***`.
laura: communication plan: notify affected customers with timeline + what we revoked and remediation steps. loop in trust+security.
sam: adding CI check to scan for env leakage: fail builds that echo ORG_ID into shared secrets.
security-bot: Incident created: SEV-HIGH-2026-03-19-CLI-ORG-LEAK. Assigned to #eng-security oncall.
maria: postmortem notes: root cause = CLI default fallback behavior change + ambiguous CI host envs. followups: (1) stricter CLI config validation, (2) token issuance guardrails in auth service, (3) KMS/encryption-at-rest audit, (4) update docs for CLI defaults.
jun: also recommend adding per-org short-lived signing keys and enforce keystore partitioning.
laura: thanks team. I'll draft customer notice and coordinate legal if needed.
maria: closing loop: roll back done, patch merged, revocations in progress, customers notified draft ready. will open a postmortem PR after primary cleanup. :white_check_mark:
